title: Faceted audit viewer: smart filters, export metadata, and RBAC-aware saved searches
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background:
We currently have a basic audit explorer but customers keep requesting higher-fidelity filtering, smaller/streamable exports, and saved queries that respect RBAC and data retention rules. This ticket implements a faceted viewer with smart filters, improved pagination tokens for large result sets, export metadata (CSV/JSON with schema headers + masking metadata), and saved searches that honor RBAC v2 permissions and SSO session context.

Goals:
- Provide a faceted search bar: actor, org, route, model, action type, resource id, date range, and user-defined tags.
- Make exports self-describing: each exported file includes a header JSON blob (as first row for CSV or top-key for JSON) that lists applied filters, client request id, export time, retention-mask version, and RBAC snapshot used to compute visible fields.
- Ensure saved queries are scoped by folder and RBAC: team-level saved queries visible only to members with the appropriate audit_read role; admin saved queries visible across orgs when allowed.
- Support streaming exports for large result sets (cursor-based + export chunking) and abort tokens for the UI.
- Add server-side throttling and export quotas to prevent runaway exports from consuming Dedicated capacity.

Design notes / Trade-offs:
- We will use the existing incremental export job infra (ENG-20345) but add a metadata envelope per chunk so downstream consumers can reconstruct ordering and schema changes. This avoids a big refactor of storage.
- Saved queries will store the filter expression and a fingerprint of the RBAC policy at save-time. On load, we will validate the current user/role against the fingerprint and either allow a read-only preview or require the user to re-evaluate the query. This prevents accidental leakage when roles change.
- To avoid leaking PII, exports adhere to the retention/masking service: fields flagged by retention policy are redacted and the export header includes the masking version.
- Pagination uses opaque cursors that include a server-signed HMAC to prevent client tampering and to carry a lightweight ordering token for consistent reads.

Acceptance criteria (must pass QA):
- UI: faceted filter panel implemented with autosuggest for actor/org/model; date-range quick presets; tag management; saved query create/edit/delete with folder selection and RBAC enforcement.
- Export: CSV and NDJSON exports include a metadata header containing applied filters, export_id, export_time, retention_mask_version, and rbac_snapshot_id. For CSV the header is a single JSON record prefixed with a hash comment (#) so tools skip it.
- Streaming: large exports (>100k rows) stream as chunked NDJSON, each chunk preceded by the same metadata envelope and sequence id; the UI shows progress and supports canceling.
- RBAC: saved queries created by a user inherit folder permissions; attempting to access a saved query without sufficient audit_read returns 403 and an explanation.
- Security review: security sign-off obtained and threat model updated to reflect export quotas and cursor signing.
- Observability: add metrics for export_count, export_bytes, export_cancel_rate, saved_query_usage, and save_query_acl_violations; dashboards linked in attachments.

Rollout plan:
1) Backend API-only feature behind feature flag audit_facets_v1. Deploy to staging and run synthetic job with 1M events.
2) Enable streaming export for internal teams and collect telemetry for 48 hours.
3) Gradually open UI to 10% of orgs, monitor export throttles and error rates for 72 hours.
4) Full rollout to all hosts, with postrollout review one week after full enablement.

QA / Test cases:
- Verify exported metadata contains accurate filter JSON and retention_mask_version matches retention service for masked fields.
- Confirm RBAC snapshot prevents stale-scope leakage: change a user's roles and ensure previously saved queries respect new permissions.
- Load test exports to ensure server-side throttles trigger at configured quota.
- Validate cursor tampering is detected (invalid signature leads to 400).

Links / artifacts:
- Spec doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/Audit+Facets+Spec
- Implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7892
- Telemetry dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/exports/exports-overview
- Threat model: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/Audit+Export+Threat+Model

Notes for reviewers:
- Reviewers should pay special attention to the export metadata schema and the RBAC snapshot semantics. We must ensure the snapshot is minimal (policy_version + role_ids) and cannot be used to reconstruct broader policy state.
- UX: ensure the metadata header format is easy to skip for analysts but robust for programmatic consumers.

2026-03-03 - Miguel Torres: Implemented server-side cursor signing and export metadata envelope. Uploaded prototype export job to staging. Noted a perf regression with 1M events - investigating batching improvements.

2026-03-07 - SRE (Jordan Lee): Observed spike in export memory when concurrent exports exceed 8. Suggested limiting concurrent exports per org and adding circuit breaker. Added ENG-26002 as a follow-up for quota enforcement tuning.
